assertions.notes: Guest 'Erasure B6' (gst_b9e97ad5-5211-4ec9-b4a2-d1db9c139555, +1555555261, rsv-b6-erase@example.com) was created by a phone booking (the Guestbook has no create-guest UI); tag 'Window seat' and the note 'B6 erasure validator note (private)' were added through the Guestbook profile UI. Erase was triggered from the profile (Erase guest -> confirm dialog) as kody: network POST http://localhost:3007/operator/reservations/guests/gst_b9e97ad5-.../erase -> 200. Profile afterwards renders 'Erased guest' with the 'This guest was erased' notice; DOM check: no old name, phone, email, tag or note (hasOldName/hasPhone/hasEmail/hasTag/hasNote all false), 2 visit-history rows remain. DB after: first_name Erased, last_name guest, phone_e164/email_norm/allergy_notes NULL, erased_at set, 0 tag rows, 0 note rows. Search returns nothing: UI search for 'Erasure B6', '+1555555261' and 'rsv-b6-erase@example.com' each showed 'No guests match your search'; server-side GET /operator/reservations/guests?q=... (guests token) returned 0 rows for all three. The erased id still opens: document GET /acme/reservations/guests/gst_b9e97ad5... -> 200 and tenant-api GET .../guests/gst_b9e97ad5... -> 200, no error state. Console errors: none for the whole browser session (agent-browser errors -> {"errors":[]}).
assertions.limitations: The contract says 'create a validator guest ... then erase them from the Guestbook UI'; the guest row itself can only be created by a booking (no direct guest-create UI), so creation was a public Sites phone booking (no sign-in) and tag+note were added in the Guestbook. Erased guests are excluded from the Guestbook list query (isNull(erased_at), rsv-guestbook-service.ts:321), so the erased guest cannot appear in list searches at all; the profile remains reachable by direct id, which is how the id-opens check was done.

assertions.notes: 1) Slot recorded: 2026-11-07 19:00 (localMin 1140, party 2, service R2-API-Service) on table G9-2 (tbl_00d903ae-8845-4460-aaa0-418a52714815, the only table of G9-Area-Strict). Remaining occurrences are inside the regional tenant DB (none in the guest row any more) and the dev email capture folder (3 files), plus the US node's own log lines ([OCI EMAIL MOCK] To: rsv-b6-erase@example.com). 4) Erased manage link: the old manage token (rsv_m_..., 104 chars) is refused by tenant-api GET http://localhost:3007/reservations/manage with X-Reservation-Token -> 404 {"error":"not_found"}, while the control token of a non-erased booking of the same shape/length returns 200; the Sites manage page opened with the erased token shows 'We could not find that reservation. The link may have expired.' and its tenant-api call is 404. The origin the captured email link points at (http://localhost:3001/reserve/manage) also 404s in local dev - the known siteOrigin/BASE_URL defect, not re-diagnosed.
assertions.limitations: The availability engine's per-slot 'preferred area' is shared state and shifted between calls while other validators booked; the decisive capacity evidence is the occupancy row (active 1 -> 0) plus the post-erase hold probe (201), not the slot count (which stayed 28 because other areas had capacity). A past booking cannot be created on Sites (slots are future-only), so the past booking was created through the operator Book screen and marked finished. The privacy sweep greps the raw sqlite files as a supplemental all-tables check; WAL contents were included for data.db (the -wal file was grepped too).

frictions.description: The Guestbook has no create-guest UI; guests can only be created by bookings (resolveOrCreateGuestForBooking). VAL-GUEST-023/024 assume a guest can be created directly in the Guestbook.
frictions.resolution: Created the validator guest through a public Sites phone booking (no sign-in) and added the tag and note through the Guestbook profile UI; documented in the assertion notes.

frictions.description: A past-date booking cannot be created through Sites (public availability only offers future slots), but VAL-CROSS-020 asks for one future and one past booking created on Sites.
frictions.resolution: Created the past booking through the operator Book screen (phone channel) and marked it booked -> seated -> finished, which is the realistic staff path and keeps its history.

frictions.description: The availability payload's preferred area per slot is unstable while other validators book; before/after comparisons can show an area change that is not caused by the booking under test.
frictions.resolution: Used the reservation's rsv_table_occupancies row (active=1 -> 0) and a post-erase hold probe on the exact slot (201) as the decisive capacity evidence, with the availability payloads as corroboration.

frictions.description: The day feed does not serialize cancelled_by, so the cancelled_by='restaurant' clause cannot be read from the Book/day-feed payload.
frictions.resolution: Verified cancelled_by='restaurant' read-only in the tenant DB and reported the day feed's status/cancelReason fields as the API-level evidence.

frictions.description: Erased guests are hidden from the Guestbook list query (isNull(erased_at)), so the anonymized guest never appears in list views or list searches; only the direct profile URL works.
frictions.resolution: Confirmed the id-still-opens clause by navigating directly to /acme/reservations/guests/<id> (document 200, profile GET 200) and treated the empty search results as expected behaviour.

frictions.description: The manage link inside captured emails points at the App origin (http://localhost:3001/reserve/manage#t=...) and 404s in local dev; only the Sites origin serves the manage page.
frictions.resolution: Known defect (do not re-diagnose). Reported both origins precisely and proved the erased token itself is refused by tenant-api (404) against a control token (200).

frictions.description: The browser's public booking requests share the tenant-api 'unknown' client bucket (book_ip 20/day) with other validators, and the Sites UI cannot set X-Forwarded-For.
frictions.resolution: Used the Sites UI for the single required public booking and created the two extra booking-created guests for VAL-GUEST-026 through curl with a private X-Forwarded-For identity (10.26.3.1).
